columns.name: customerID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each customer (not used for modeling).

columns.name: gender
columns.description: Customer's gender.

columns.name: SeniorCitizen
columns.description: Whether the customer is a senior citizen (1) or not (0).

columns.name: Partner
columns.description: Whether the customer has a partner.

columns.name: Dependents
columns.description: Whether the customer has dependents.

columns.name: tenure
columns.description: Number of months the customer has stayed with the company.

columns.name: PhoneService
columns.description: Whether the customer has phone service.

columns.name: MultipleLines
columns.description: Whether the customer has multiple phone lines.

columns.name: InternetService
columns.description: Customer's internet service type.

columns.name: OnlineSecurity
columns.description: Whether the customer has online security add-on.

columns.name: OnlineBackup
columns.description: Whether the customer has online backup add-on.

columns.name: DeviceProtection
columns.description: Whether the customer has device protection add-on.

columns.name: TechSupport
columns.description: Whether the customer has tech support add-on.

columns.name: StreamingTV
columns.description: Whether the customer has streaming TV service.

columns.name: StreamingMovies
columns.description: Whether the customer has streaming movies service.

columns.name: Contract
columns.description: The customer's contract term.

columns.name: PaperlessBilling
columns.description: Whether the customer uses paperless billing.

columns.name: PaymentMethod
columns.description: The customer's payment method.

columns.name: MonthlyCharges
columns.description: The amount charged to the customer monthly.

columns.name: TotalCharges
columns.description: The total amount charged to the customer over their tenure.

columns.name: Churn
columns.description: Whether the customer churned (left the company).

cleaning_notes: TotalCharges was stored as text and converted to numeric; 11 blank values that resulted were filled with the column median.
customerID was dropped before modeling — it carries no predictive signal.
Binary columns (gender, Partner, Dependents, PhoneService, PaperlessBilling) were label-encoded; multi-category columns were one-hot encoded with the first category dropped to avoid redundancy.
Only the three continuous numeric columns (tenure, MonthlyCharges, TotalCharges) were scaled with StandardScaler, fit on the training set only to prevent data leakage.
